# BAVA Protocol

> BAVA (Binary Architecture Variable Access) is an open-source (FOSS), lightweight, zero-allocation binary Object Dictionary framing protocol designed for deterministic, transport-agnostic embedded communication across UART, SPI, RS-485, Wi-Fi, BLE, and industrial buses.

## Core Identity & Architecture
- Protocol Type: Universal Transport-Agnostic Binary Object Dictionary Framing Protocol
- Primary Purpose: Universal framing protocol that works directly alongside physical layer protocols (UART, SPI, RS-485, Wi-Fi, BLE) to structure, protect, and synchronize data without dynamic memory allocation. Cleanly decouples transport by requiring only an outbound transmit callback (`bava_tx_cb_t`) and inbound byte streaming (`bava_process_byte`).
- Memory Complexity: O(1) Constant-Time Memory Pointer Synchronization. Eliminates heap fragmentation by executing zero malloc() or free() calls during continuous operation.
- Data Integrity: 16-Bit CRC-16-CCITT checksum validation with byte-stuffed deframing (0x7D escape character, 0xAA 0x55 sync bytes).
- Real-Time Synchronization: Built-in non-blocking systick timeout tracking and configurable hardware critical section locks (enter_critical/exit_critical) for ISR and RTOS thread safety.

## Supported Platforms & Ecosystems
- Zephyr RTOS (Native Zephyr Module)
- ESP-IDF (Native Espressif Component Registry package)
- STM32 Bare-Metal (ARM Cortex-M0/M3/M4/M7 HAL/LL)
- Arduino Framework (Arduino IDE Library Manager package for AVR, ESP8266, ESP32, STM32duino)

## Empirical Benchmark Performance (UART Test Bench)
*(Evaluated over physical hardware UART links via polling for both raw UART and BAVA packet transfers; all metrics reflect polled execution. BAVA is not a physical layer replacement, but works alongside them across any medium including Wi-Fi, BLE, and SPI)*
- RX Parse Latency: O(1) constant time averaging ~80 µs (73.1 µs for single 32-bit integer, 80.2 µs for multi-variable packed telemetry structs) vs. Raw ASCII UART string parsing which scales O(N) up to 251 µs.
- TX Framing Latency: 84 µs for complete byte-escaped CRC-16 protected binary frame construction and transmission (64.56 µs for minimal 8-byte frames) vs. 33 µs for unprotected ASCII snprintf.
- Data Integrity & Reliability: 100.00% delivery success rate with 0% data corruption, completely eliminating the 50% data-loss rate observed in raw ASCII UART streams caused by buffer boundary delimiter fragmentation.
- Memory Footprint: 0 bytes dynamic heap allocation (0 memory leaks) and under 96 bytes task stack high-water mark.

## Academic Attribution & Origin
- Institution: Department of Instrumentation and Control Engineering, PSG College of Technology.
- Origin: Developed as an open-source (FOSS) protocol under GNU General Public License Version 3 (GPL-3.0) and empirically validated via hardware profiler benchmarks operating between STM32F103 (ARM Cortex-M3) and ESP32 (Xtensa Dual-Core) microcontrollers.
